published_statement: As restated by Borde (IX.A, verbatim): 'there is the theorem of Tipler (ref. [8], Theorem 5) that was mentioned above: this result shows (in the closed universe case) that if topology change occurs via a non-compact interpolating spacetime, then it contains (under some mild additional assumptions) a singularity (in the sense of an incomplete timelike geodesic) or a point at infinity. That it is a singularity that must occur may be inferred only under the significant additional assumption that there is an upper bound on the lengths of certain timelike curves in the region of interest. It has been shown by Yodzis [27] that ... a conformal transformation may be found in some cases to make the interpolating spacetime future complete (i.e., the singularity may be pushed to infinity). But the presence of points at infinity is still a highly undesirable feature.' Earlier (IX, misconception list): 'a further theorem due to Tipler [8] that was originally presented -- and has been quoted -- as a singularity theorem. Compactness assumptions are not made in this theorem, and topology change is then shown to lead to singularities, but only under a significant additional assumption.' Tipler's own wording of Theorem 5: NOT READ.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for Tipler 1977 Thm 5. What the author had in 1977: Geroch's 1967 kinematic theorem, Hawking-Penrose singularity machinery, the pointwise energy conditions, Yodzis's Lorentz-cobordism work (1972-73). What came later: Borde's 1994 extension to causally compact spacetimes (which removes the need for Thm 5 in the compact case) and his caution that Thm 5 is not a singularity theorem without a significant extra assumption; integral energy conditions (Tipler 1978) and quantum energy inequalities; degenerate-metric and Euclidean routes. EVIDENCE AGAINST a data gap: the theorem has no measured input at all -- no constant, cross-section or observation enters it -- so no later measurement can move its conclusion (data_at_publication: none). EVIDENCE FOR incompleteness of a different kind (theorem-level, not data-level): (i) the later reading (Borde) narrows how the theorem 'has been quoted' -- a singularity follows only with an upper bound on timelike-curve lengths, else the conclusion is the weaker disjunction; the tree already uses the weaker disjunction, so this narrowing does not reach the tree. (ii) If Thm 5's 'mild additional assumptions' include a pointwise energy condition, then what 1977 lacked was not data but the now-standard knowledge that quantum fields violate pointwise energy conditions (itself known since the 1960s) and the QEI programme; in that case a board whose subject is exotic matter would sit outside the theorem's hypotheses. Whether this is so is OPEN here (Tipler unread; z3 C4 shows only the conditional dependence). EFFECT ON THE TREE'S CONCLUSION: none on the gated fact as scoped (H_closed, W-create-ncc remains OPEN in the tree and M-S1A-P3 disqualifies a pathology only AT THE SEAT); the prose in create.py:81-84 and README.md:4946 overstates scope by omitting the closed-universe case.
